title: <thinking> text included in code when using ollama
description:
Summary:
Code only output for ollama local model no longer work for `gander` 0.2.0 when using `ellmer` 0.4.2. gander works well with `ellmer` 0.4.0.

Details:
When in R script, highlighting an R object (or from scratch) -> ctrl+alt+G -> prompt, I expect the output should be only code.

This works with `options(gander.chat = ellmer::chat_ollama(...)` with `gander` 0.2.0 and `ellmer` 0.4.0 combination. But, it no longer works with `ellmer` 0.4.2, where it outputs content of `<thinking></thinking>`.

This works with `gander` 0.2.0 + `ellmer` 0.4.0:
```r
options(
  gander.chat = ellmer::chat_ollama(
    base_url = Sys.getenv("OLLAMA_BASE_URL", "http://localhost:11434"),
    model = "qwen-64k", # qwen3.8 with 64k num_ctx
    api_args = list(
      generationConfig = list(
        thinkingConfig = list(thinkingLevel = "minimal")
      )
    )
  )
)
```
But it no longer works with ellmer 0.4.2.

I tried adjusting with ellmer's new options `echo="none"` and `params = params(reasoning_effort = ...)`:
```r
options(
  gander.chat = ellmer::chat_ollama(
    base_url = Sys.getenv("OLLAMA_BASE_URL", "http://localhost:11434"),
    model = "qwen-64k", # qwen3.8 with 64k num_ctx
    echo = "none", # gander SHOULD not output thinking, but not working right now
    params = params(reasoning_effort = "minimal"),
    # params = params(reasoning_effort = "none") # this works even without echo = "none"
  )
)
```
But gander still outputs content of thinking tag. This will only work if I set `params(reasoning_effort = "none")`, which means no thinking steps are involved and will degrade the quality of the outputs.

I attach `gander_peek()` and inline output for your reference:

`gander_peek()`:
```text
The user made the following request:

> Load mtcars builtin dataset as data
── assistant [input=824 output=40] ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
<thinking>
The user wants me to provide R code that loads the mtcars dataset as an object named `data`, using tidyverse style.
</thinking>

data <- as_tibble(mtcars)
```

Inline output of gander:
```text
The user wants me to provide R code that loads the mtcars dataset as an object named `data`, using tidyverse style.data <- as_tibble(mtcars)
```

Expected inline text:
```text
data <- as_tibble(mtcars)
```

Best regards

title: engineer prompt to clarify the agent's task
description:
I think we can do some prompt engineering to make the models understand their task much more clearly when situated inside of gander's harness. 

If I'm in this package's description file and select just the version and then say "bump this," this is what I see:

`````
> gander::gander_peek()
<Chat Anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 turns=3 input=723 output=11>
── system ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
You are a helpful but terse R data scientist. When asked for code, provide only the requested code, no exposition nor backticks, unless explicitly asked. Always provide a minimal solution and refrain from unnecessary additions. Use tidyverse style and, when relevant, tidyverse packages. For example, when asked to plot something, use ggplot2, or when asked to transform data, using dplyr and/or tidyr unless explicitly instructed otherwise. 
── user ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Up to this point, the contents of my  file reads: 

```
Package: gander
Title: High Performance, Low Friction Large Language Model Chat
```

Now, bump this: 

```
Version: 0.1.0.9000
```

For context, the rest of the file reads: 

```
Authors@R: c(
    person("Simon", "Couch", , "simon.couch@posit.co", role = c("aut", "cre"),
           comment = c(ORCID = "0000-0001-5676-5107")),
    person("Posit Software, PBC", role = c("cph", "fnd"))
  )
Description: Introduces a 'Copilot'-like completion experience, but it knows how
    to talk to the objects in your R environment. 'ellmer' chats are integrated 
    directly into your 'RStudio' and 'Positron' sessions, automatically 
    incorporating relevant context from surrounding lines of code and your
    global environment (like data frame columns and types). Open the package 
    dialog box with a keyboard shortcut, type your request, and the assistant 
    will stream its response directly into your documents.
License: MIT + file LICENSE
Config/testthat/edition: 3
Encoding: UTF-8
Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)
RoxygenNote: 7.3.3
URL: https://github.com/simonpcouch/gander, https://simonpcouch.github.io/gander/
BugReports: https://github.com/simonpcouch/gander/issues
Depends:
    R (>= 4.3.0)
Imports: 
    cli (>= 3.6.3),
    glue (>= 1.8.0),
    ellmer (>= 0.2.0),
    miniUI (>= 0.1.1.1),
    rlang (>= 1.1.4),
    rstudioapi (>= 0.17.1),
    shiny (>= 1.9.1),
    streamy (>= 0.1.0.9000),
    treesitter,
    treesitter.r
Suggests: 
    gt,
    knitr,
    rmarkdown,
    testthat (>= 3.0.0),
    tibble,
    withr
Remotes:
    simonpcouch/streamy
VignetteBuilder: knitr

```
── assistant [input=723 output=11] ────────────────────────────────
Version: 0.1.1
`````

Right now, the package tries to situate the prompt as if it actually was written by the user. We should reformat it to just be explicit about what the task is. 

* The "bump this" is situated in natural language. It should just be prefixed with "The user has provided with the following request"
* The package uses triple backticks to show the selected region. It should use five backticks instead.
* The prompt ends with the full file state, via: "For context, the rest of the file reads:"

We should rewrite to:

* File context, five-backticked, prefixed with "The user is currently working in this file"
* Then, write: "The user made the following request" and put it in blockquotes >
* Then, write: "The user has made the following selection that they're like to apply the request to:" and put the relevant selection in five backticks.
* Also rewrite the system prompt, probably just by appending to it, to tell the agent what its task is, which is to apply the request to the selection. 

Instead, this example should read something like:

**System:**

```
You are a helpful but terse R data scientist. When asked for code, provide only the requested code, no exposition nor backticks, unless explicitly asked. Always provide a minimal solution and refrain from unnecessary additions. Use tidyverse style and, when relevant, tidyverse packages. For example, when asked to plot something, use ggplot2, or when asked to transform data, using dplyr and/or tidyr unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

Your task is to apply the user's request to their selected text. Return only the replacement text for the selection—no surrounding context, no explanation, no backticks.
```

title: Consider clarifying privacy discussion in documentation
description:
Very cool package here - thanks for the great work.

I am wondering if the data values themselves are passed into gander at any point, or whether it's just a summary/description (i.e., column names, variable distributions, moments, etc). This is crucial to know for those of us working with data protected by company privacy rules or privacy laws (e.g., with HIPAA-protected data).

In the documentation within https://simonpcouch.github.io/gander, it says, "_...[gander allows] for models to pick up on the names, types, and distributions of the variables it may work with..._" and "_...gander automatically passes along your code and the objects in your R environment to your chosen model._" 

Names, types, and distributions are fine for those of us who don't keep sensitive data in the column names (and aren't worried about identifiability of distributions). But if raw values from the data (e.g., `head(data)` or similar functions) are run behind the scenes, the results of these would be problematic to feed into a public LLM.  Would you mind clarifying here (and perhaps also in the documentation for everyone else as well)? Thanks!

title: Add context to LLMs completion
description:
It would be really nice if gander could read from package's topic help pages to get context for a problem.

In my company, we have internally developed R packages that we use in conjunction with open-source packages, and our code-generation attempts often fail because the LLM of course doesn't know about our frameworks (and our colleagues are too busy to learn them haha). 

In https://github.com/MichelNivard/GPTstudio they've got this nice feature in their chat window where you can type in something like "dplyr::mutate" in your prompt. There's some regex behind it to pull out these "package/topic pairs" and retrieve the help doc, parse it, and then pass it to the LLMs context along with the rest of your prompt. 

This works very nicely for code generation, as the LLM can get the function signatures perfect when paired with a good model like claude 3.5. The only thing its missing is what gander provides with the R environment integration. As they're working as a background process, it will likely be very difficult to implement what gander is doing, but relatively trivial for gander to implement what they're doing (I can only assume :)). 

What do you think? I would be happy to help build this out.

title: FEAT REQUEST: context, fix privacy while maintaining usability
description:
Great package, I wrote a short blog (in dutch) about the rise of programming languages vs low-code tools due to llms (that are much more helpful with R and python than they are with Tableau for instance). I included the gif of this repo as an illustration. 

gander currently has the following method of adding info about a dataframe to the context when the dataframe is send with the prompt:

```
  if (inherits(x, "data.frame")) {
    n_row <- min(5, nrow(x))
    n_col <- min(20, ncol(x))
    x <- x[seq_len(n_row), seq_len(n_col), drop = FALSE]
    x_name <- c(
      cli::format_inline("# Just the first {n_row} row{?s} and {n_col} column{?s}:"),
      x_name
    )
  }
```

My suggestion is either a summary per variable or just a class. Potential with the mode value if that helps. 
- The rows while only 5 still give a potential privacy issue (since you have up to 20 columns of the first row). 
- When only supporting 20 cols without the possibility ot set it higher, it can lead to difficult to debug issues  (why doesn't gander get variable x, it did j fine). If you have 150 cols the summary or class would still be okay within the context window while maintaining privacy.

title: Feature request: local network ollama; handling <think> yapping
description:
Thank you for this great addition to RStudio! I'm testing it out using a local llm with 'thinking' abilities, and the verboseness in qmd files is extraordinary. However, it does get 'covered' in <think> </think> tags, so I'm curious if the function keep that part out of the end-result could be eliminated (or commented). Secondly, would it be possible to setup so that one can use a network url for the ollama instance?

All the best,

title: remove `Context` selectize
description:
Initially, with an eye for privacy, I implemented the `Context` dropdown so that users could _just_ send their code selection to models. I don't think this is the way to go in that 1) it's too easy for users to mistakenly send code context they didn't mean to (especially when they're starting out) and 2) there'd need to be a related toggle for context from the environment.

I think the safer, simpler, and more powerful way to go here is to always include a consistent set of code and environment context and instruct users to choose `gander_fn` appropriately according to their privacy needs.

* fetch image (if you see a URL or file path to image, request it and I'll load it in and pass it via `content_image_*()`
* [pkgprompt](https://github.com/simonpcouch/pkgprompt) kinda thing--show me the docs for a package or function. Would be curious if Edgar's LLM translation package would have some good utilities for loading help-files as markdown
